newsitem.title: UK: Currency dominates at European vegetable oil close.
newsitem.headline: Currency dominates at European vegetable oil close.

text.p: A lower dollar against the guilder counteracted the higher Chicago on the European vegetable oil market on Monday afternoon.
Soft oil sellers trimmed prices during the afternoon to finish with soy oil one guilder down to unchanged while rape oil was 0.75 down to 0.50 up at the close.
However, lower prices failed to drum up much business with one trade reported in soy oil at 103.50 guilders per 100 kilos for May and one in rape oil at 104.50 guilders for the same position.
"Neither trade had much volume behind it and they came out of the blue because there were no bids against the positions," said one trader.
Palm oil closed mostly higher with sellers taking their cue from the firm close in Malaysia.
Higher Chicago futures on Friday, good export data and local tightness in the physical market were behind the rise in Malaysia.
Malaysian cargo surveyor Societe Generale de Surveillance (SGS) on Monday estimated exports for April 1-20 at 429,661 tonnes against 391,599 tonnes in March 1-20.

However, European traders said the upside of the market was limited by rising Malaysian output and a slowdown in export business with many of Malaysia's traditional customers buying soft oils at the expense of palm oil.
Malaysian private forecaster Ivan Wong in his latest report projected April output at 723,000 tonnes, a rise of six percent.
Some traders said this was about in line with the steady build up in output they expected ahead of the peak months of October/November.
However, others said it was towards the lower end of expectations.
At the close crude palm oil cif Europe was $2.50 to $5 higher after May fetched $562.50 and $565 in early trading.
RBD palm oil was $2.50 higher while olein offers were $2.50 to $5 up after May traded at $592.50. $597.50 and $595.
Full June traded at $585 while dated June fetched $582.50 and $583 and Jul $575 and $577.50 a tonne fob Malaysian ports.
Lauric oils were quiet with coconut oil unchanged to $5 up and palmkernel oil $2.50 to $5 higher in neglected markets.
